intro: Lesson 41: 3.2 How Salah is performed: movements and recitations. To understand the movements and recitations of salah and their meaning

questions.q: Explain why sujud is significant in salah. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: It is the position closest to Allah (Muslim) and shows total submission: the forehead, the highest part, on the ground.
questions.model: Point 1: it brings closeness to Allah. Develop: 'the closest a servant is to his Lord is in sujud' (Muslim). Point 2: it shows humility. Develop: the forehead on the ground expresses submission, the meaning of Islam.

questions.q: In the portal response box: 'Describe how a Muslim performs two rak'ahs of Fajr.' Include movements and recitations in order. Start: 'After making wudu and facing the qiblah, ...'
questions.a: Correct sequence: niyyah, takbir, Fatihah and surah, ruku', i'tidal, two sujud, second rak'ah, tashahhud, taslim
questions.model: Teacher writes the opening: 'After making wudu and facing the qiblah, the Muslim makes the niyyah and says Allahu akbar, raising the hands.'

questions.q: what does each movement show about the relationship with Allah?
questions.a: Standing: readiness; bowing: respect; sujud: submission; sitting: calm testimony.

questions.q: why is al-Fatihah called the 'mother of the Book'?
questions.a: It sums up the Qur'an's themes: praise, worship, guidance.

questions.q: Back to our ponder: why do movements say more than words?
questions.a: The body shows submission; sujud is closest to Allah.
